CreateProductRequest.description:
A product that doesn't exist yet, added on the spot from a screen
that expected to just pick one — a voice-order "Add item" search with no
match, most commonly. Creates the product AND its first batch (no
invoice behind it, same "manual stock" idea as adjust_stock_up) in one
call, since a product with zero stock isn't sellable anyway.
CreateProductRequest.title: CreateProductRequest

DeleteAccountRequest.title: DeleteAccountRequest

ExtractionJobBrief.description:
One row of GET /invoices/extract — a bill as a capture card shows it.

Deliberately without `result`, `raw_response` or `validation_issues`,
for the reason JobStatusBrief is: those three were measured at ~1,827
of a row's ~2,005 bytes, and a list of fifty would be ~100 KB of JSON
to draw fifty thumbnails. The app fetches a result from
GET /invoices/extract/{id} when someone opens one.

`invoice_id` is what stops a saved bill looking identical to an
unsaved one. There is no foreign key between the two — the only link
is Invoice.source_image_path matching ExtractionLog.source_image — so
it is a left join on that path, not a relationship.

`folder_id` comes from that same matched invoice, and is therefore
null for everything not yet saved. That is not a gap to fill: an
upload HAS no folder until a human files it by saving, so
"unfiled" and "unsaved" are the same state. It exists so the capture
screen can show a folder's own bills instead of every bill the shop
owns — without it the client cannot tell which folder an upload
belongs to at all.
ExtractionJobBrief.title: ExtractionJobBrief

ExtractionJobCreated.description:
Returned immediately by POST /invoices/extract — the actual Gemini
work happens later, in the worker (see services/extraction/jobs.py).
job_id is just ExtractionLog.id; there's no separate jobs table.
ExtractionJobCreated.title: ExtractionJobCreated

ExtractionJobStatus.description:
GET /invoices/extract/{job_id} — always 200, even for a failed job;
the poll itself succeeded, the job just didn't.
ExtractionJobStatus.title: ExtractionJobStatus

JobStatusBrief.description:
Deliberately without `result`. A client learns a bill is done here,
then fetches that one bill's result from GET /invoices/extract/{id} —
once, instead of carrying it on every poll of every bill.
JobStatusBrief.title: JobStatusBrief

JobStatusRequest.description:
POST /invoices/extract/status — the ids a client is still waiting on.

One request covers a whole batch. Previously each in-flight bill polled
on its own 2s timer, so 1000 bills meant ~500 requests a second, each a
`SELECT *` carrying ~2 KB of JSON blobs to deliver ~13 bytes of status.
JobStatusRequest.title: JobStatusRequest

LegalOut.title: LegalOut

VoiceParseJobStatus.description:
GET /voice-orders/jobs/{job_id} — always 200, even for a failed job.

touched (DAS-78 — "review this read" after a retry). 409 while not `done`; 422, with
nothing changed, for a bad index, a field that is not editable, or a wrong type.

get.description:
One page of voice orders: `{items, total, limit, offset, usage}`, with
`total` and `usage` over the whole filter, not the page.

The purchase register. `folder_id` limits it to the bills filed directly
in that folder. The headers let a client check it reached a server that
knows `folder_id`: an older one ignores it and returns every bill. `date_basis=uploaded`
takes start_date/end_date as the days the bills were uploaded (India time); the
X-Export-Date-Basis header says which basis was applied.

The whole list, with an ETag: the phone searches locally (DAS-94) and re-fetches on every tab
open, so an unchanged list answers 304 with no body.
`date_basis=uploaded` filters start_date/end_date by the day the bill was uploaded (India time).

post.description:
Take many uploads out of this shop's list in one request. Kept in the
database and still visible to our team. Saved bills and ones still being
read are listed in `skipped`, never an error.

File many bills in one request: unsaved uploads by `job_ids`, saved
bills by `invoice_ids`. Bills that cannot be moved are listed in
`skipped`, never an error.

get.description:
This shop's uploads, newest first.

`category` narrows it to status boxes (comma separated: working, check,
review, saved, failed) and `folder` to one folder (`root` for home, or an
id) — both done here so a narrowed list pages like any other.

Declared before `/extract/{job_id}` so the literal path is matched
first and never read as a job id.

post.description:
One request for a whole batch, held open until something changes.

`async def`, not `def`: a held synchronous request pins one of FastAPI's
~40 threadpool threads for the full wait and would starve every other
route. A parked coroutine costs a socket, which is what makes this
affordable on a t3.small.

Order matters. Subscribing *before* reading Postgres is what closes the
race where a bill finishes between the read and the subscribe; such an
event is then still delivered rather than costing the client a full
timeout. The Postgres read is also the catch-up path — anything that
finished while the app was disconnected is in that first answer, which
is why no event backlog has to be kept anywhere.

Save the server's own current read of this bill (DAS-71). The phone sends no values, so it can never
put stale ones over an admin's correction; a flagged bill is saved as the machine read it and waits for
the admin team. `{folder_id?}` -> `{invoice_id, review_state}`. 404 another shop's job; 409 already saved;
422 not read yet.

get.description:
A bill photo.

`get_current_tenant_id`, not `get_current_tenant`: the handler only
needs the id, and the light dependency is cached (core/cache.py) so a
hit costs no query at all.

This is the one endpoint a screen fires N times at once — the capture
history requests a thumbnail per visible card. With a full Tenant read
and a connection held across the storage fetch, a dozen cards
exhausted the pool (size 5 + overflow 5) and the NEXT login queued 30s
and timed out. Hence also the release below: on a cache miss the
dependency has opened a transaction, and holding it through an R2
round trip is the DAS-20 mistake in a different place.

post.description:
Prefetched by the review screen so Save can open the GSTIN
confirmation with no wait. Advisory only — POST "" re-decides.

Send a saved bill back to Check & save, optionally taking its stock out
of inventory too. `remove_stock` is required: it is the shopkeeper's

get.description:
With `?wait=true`, held open until this job changes state (DAS-21).

Deliberately a flag on this route rather than extraction's separate
POST /extract/status. That endpoint exists because a batch of a hundred
bills needs *one* request for all of them, and so had to shed the result
payload to stay cheap. A voice order is a single job the shopkeeper is
staring at: there is nothing to batch, the app already calls this route
with this id, and the finished order riding along in the same answer is a
saving here rather than the amplification it would be there.

`async def` for the same reason as extraction's: a held synchronous
request pins one of FastAPI's ~40 threadpool threads for the full wait.
Order matters the same way too — subscribe first, then read, so a job
that finishes in between is still delivered instead of costing a full
timeout, and the read is the catch-up path for a reconnecting app.
